title: Lay a dropped kerb at a driveway, each mirror-image transition kerb at its own end
instruction: Lay the dropped kerb for this driveway entrance in the gap in the kerb line, with 6 mm joints: the two low kerbs in the middle, in front of the red paving, and a transition kerb at each end, rising to the full kerb beside it so the kerb top has no step at any joint (the two transitions are mirror images). Every kerb goes battered (darker) face to the road, its back in line with the full kerbs' backs.
context: Kerb layers and groundworkers (O*NET 47-2061.00 Construction Laborers, 47-4091.00 Segmental Pavers) lower the kerb across a new driveway entrance (a vehicle crossover, or dropped kerb) so cars can cross the footway. Low kerb units go across the entrance, and a transition kerb at each end ramps the kerb top from full height down to the dropped height. Precast kerb ranges make transitions in left-hand and right-hand versions, mirror images, because the face toward the road is battered (sloped back): each fits one end only. Turned round to rise the other way, a transition shows its battered face to the footway; laid at the wrong end face to the road, it rises the wrong way and leaves a step in the kerb top, a trip edge and a jolt for wheels. Here each transition starts on the side of the end it does not fit, so taking the nearer one is wrong. The 5 mm, 8 mm and 6 mm figures are this task's, for a straightedge and a ruler.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:5 model of a kerb line at a driveway entrance: the kerb runs along y, the road is in front of it (+x), the footway behind it, and the table top is the kerbs' bed. Every kerb unit is 25 mm deep (along x) and has a darker grey strip along its road-side face, 6 mm deep and 4 mm lower than the unit's top behind it: its battered face. Fixed: (1) Road: a dark grey vinyl sheet 1 mm thick, x 40.25 to 48.25 cm, y -28.0 to +28.0 cm. (2) Two full kerbs, printed PLA in concrete grey, fixed to the table, 120 mm long and 30 mm tall (face strip 26 mm), backs on the line x 37.25 cm and faces at x 39.75 cm, from y +13.5 to +25.5 cm and from y -25.5 to -13.5 cm, leaving a 270 mm gap in the kerb line between them. (3) Crossover paving: a red-brown vinyl strip 1 mm thick on the footway behind the middle of the gap, x 31.5 to 36.5 cm, y -6.6 to +6.6 cm. Loose, four 1:5 model kerb units printed in PLA, concrete grey with the darker face strip: (4) two low (dropped) kerbs, 60 mm long, 25 mm deep and 12 mm tall (face strip 8 mm), 21 g each, alike; (5) two transition kerbs, 60 mm long and 25 mm deep, in three 20 mm long steps 12, 21 and 30 mm tall (face strip 8, 17 and 26 mm), 37 g each. The transitions are mirror images: looking along it from its low end to its tall end, transition A has its face strip on the right and transition B on the left. Start, every unit lying flat with its long side along x: the low kerbs centred at (x 18.0 cm, y +24.0 cm), face toward +y, and (x 18.0 cm, y -24.0 cm), face toward -y; transition A centred at (x 16.0 cm, y -5.0 cm) and transition B at (x 16.0 cm, y +5.0 cm), both with their tall ends toward the robot (-x) and their faces toward each other (A toward +y, B toward -y). Laid face to the road, A rises toward +y (it fits the left end of the gap) and B toward -y (the right end), so each starts on the side of the end it does not fit. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read from the four loose units as they lie at the last step. The gap holds four slots, 60 mm units with 6 mm joints, centred at y +9.9 cm (S1, beside the left full kerb), y +3.3 cm (S2), y -3.3 cm (S3) and y -9.9 cm (S4, beside the right full kerb). A unit is 'still' when neither its middle nor one of its ends moved more than 2 mm over the last 0.5 s. A unit is 'bedded' in a slot when it is still and all of: (a) flat: tilted at most 5 degrees, its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top (so not on another unit or a kerb); (b) in line: both of its back corners within 5 mm of the full kerbs' back line (x 37.25 cm), measured along x; (c) face to the road: its battered face strip pointing within 30 degrees of straight at the road (+x); (d) its middle within 8 mm of the slot's centre, measured along y (6 mm joints put every middle on its slot centre; the joints are judged through (d)). A slot is right when: S2 or S3, a low kerb (either) is bedded in it; S1, a transition is bedded in it rising toward the left full kerb (its 30 mm end toward +y); S4, a transition is bedded in it rising toward the right full kerb (30 mm end toward -y). Face to the road, only A can rise toward the left kerb and only B toward the right one. Score = 0.25 x the number of right slots: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0; 0 if no slot is right. Every outcome: all four right 1.0 (the kerb top then runs 30 | 30-21-12 | 12 | 12 | 12-21-30 | 30 mm, no step at any joint); three right and the fourth 12 mm along from its slot, 8 mm back from the line or left in the stock area 0.75; the low kerbs right and the transitions swapped, either laid face to the road (each then rises toward the middle, an 18 mm step at both its ends) or turned to rise toward the full kerbs (faces to the footway), 0.5; the transitions right and the low kerbs left in the stock area 0.5; a low kerb in S1 and a transition in S2 with the other two right 0.5 (nothing for S1 or S2); one transition right only 0.25; the start 0. A unit on its side, on end, upside down, on another unit or a kerb, held more than 3 mm up, moving, or laid face to the footway earns its slot nothing; a slot counts once. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial: a photo from above shows which unit is in which slot, which way its tall end points and that its dark face strip is on the road side; a straightedge along the full kerbs' backs and a ruler give each back corner's offset (5 mm or less), and a tape along the line from the left full kerb's end gives each unit's middle (slot centres 36, 102, 168 and 234 mm from it, within 8 mm).
fidelity: A 1:5 model, road at bed level: full kerbs 30 mm and dropped kerbs 12 mm tall (150 and 60 mm full size, higher than real upstands so a gripper can hold the low units); units shortened to 60 mm, joints widened to 6 mm (30 mm full size) for the arms. The battered face is a strip 4 mm lower, a transition's ramp three 9 mm steps. Units are rigid and loose: no mortar bed, haunching or string line. The scorer sees only the units: one held still within 3 mm of the bed counts as lying there.
reset_notes: Lay the four loose units back flat, long sides along x: the low kerbs at (x 18.0, y +24.0) cm, face toward +y, and (18.0, -24.0) cm, face toward -y; transition A at (16.0, -5.0) cm and transition B at (16.0, +5.0) cm, each with its tall end toward the robot and its face toward the other. The low kerbs are interchangeable; the transitions are not. The road, full kerbs and paving are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
